speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To start, can you describe the nature of the swelling in your right knee, such as whether it is red, warm, or fluctuant?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the lack of trauma and family history are significant clues. Can you tell me if the swelling has been present since birth or if it appeared suddenly, and does the child have a limp or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Unilateral Hydrops of the Knee (likely due to lymphatic obstruction or lymphangioma). Given the patient's age, lack of trauma, unilateral swelling, and strong familial history, this presentation is highly suggestive of a hereditary lymphatic disorder affecting the knee joint. REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_Right_Knee.
